introduction-streams-vs-firehose.core: Kinesis Data Streams is a durable, ordered, replayable log of records split into shards. You build consumers that read at their own pace, with retention from 24 hours to 365 days. Amazon Data Firehose is a fully managed delivery pipe that buffers, optionally transforms and loads streaming data into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch or HTTP endpoints, with no consumers to write.

first_principles.problem: A team writes custom consumer code just to land clickstream data in S3.
truths: Some streams need custom real-time processing.
Many just need delivery to storage.
derivation: **Data Streams** for custom, ordered, multi-consumer real-time processing.
**Chain** them (Streams → Firehose) when you need both.

analogy.title: A conveyor belt versus a delivery service
analogy.story: The belt carries items past workers who process them; the delivery service just takes boxes to the warehouse.
analogy.breaks: Conveyor items are gone once taken; stream records can be re-read until retention expires.

example.title: Two pipelines
flow: Fraud detection reading every event in order → Data Streams + Lambda
Clickstream archive to S3 Parquet → Firehose

check.q: Which Kinesis service requires no consumer code to load data into S3?

kinesis-data-streams-sharding-physics.core: Each shard ingests up to 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s and serves 2 MB/s of reads shared by standard consumers. Records route to shards by hashing the partition key, preserving order per key. Choose provisioned shard counts or on-demand mode, and pick high-cardinality partition keys to avoid hot shards.

first_principles.problem: Producers get ProvisionedThroughputExceeded because all records use the same partition key.

analogy.title: Toll booths on a motorway
analogy.story: Each booth handles a fixed number of cars per minute; cars are assigned booths by licence plate.
analogy.breaks: Drivers can switch booths; records with the same key always go to the same shard.

check.q: What's the write limit per Kinesis shard?

enhanced-fan-out-breaking-the-read-limit.core: Standard consumers share each shard's 2 MB/s read limit and poll with GetRecords (max 5 calls/s per shard), so several consumers slow each other. Enhanced fan-out gives each registered consumer its own dedicated 2 MB/s per shard pushed over HTTP/2 (SubscribeToShard), with ~70 ms latency, at extra cost.

first_principles.problem: Adding a fourth consumer causes lag and throttling for all consumers of the stream.
truths: Shared read throughput divides among consumers.
derivation: Use **enhanced fan-out** for many or latency-sensitive consumers.

analogy.title: A shared tap versus individual taps
analogy.story: With one tap, everyone waits their turn; with individual taps, everyone fills at full speed.
analogy.breaks: Taps cost the same; each EFO consumer adds cost.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Fraud detector gets its own throughput.

check.q: How much read throughput does each EFO consumer get per shard?

kinesis-firehose-the-buffer-logic.core: Firehose buffers incoming records by size (e.g. 1–128 MB) or time (0–900 s), whichever comes first, then delivers a batch. It can transform with Lambda, convert JSON to Parquet/ORC using a Glue schema, compress, partition dynamically by record fields into S3 prefixes, and back up failed records.

first_principles.problem: Firehose writes millions of tiny files to S3, hurting Athena performance.
truths: Bigger buffers mean fewer, larger files.
derivation: Set **buffer size/interval** for file size vs latency.

analogy.title: A bus that leaves when full or on schedule
analogy.story: It waits to fill up, but never longer than the timetable allows.
analogy.breaks: Buses carry the same passengers; Firehose can transform and convert records en route.

example.title: Parquet with partitions
flow: Convert JSON → Parquet via Glue table

check.q: When does Firehose deliver a batch?
check.a: When either the buffer size or the buffer interval is reached, whichever comes first.

kinesis-vs-sqs-choosing-the-right-tool.core: Kinesis is a replayable, ordered stream that many consumers read independently, with per-shard ordering and retention. Good for analytics, event sourcing and fan-out of high-volume data. SQS is a queue where each message is processed once by one consumer group and deleted, with per-message visibility, DLQs and simpler scaling. Good for task distribution.

first_principles.problem: A team uses SQS for analytics events that three teams need to read, duplicating queues and losing replay.
truths: Streams retain data; queues delete on consumption.
Replays help recovery and new consumers.
derivation: **Kinesis** for multiple consumers, ordering, replay, high throughput.
**SQS** for job queues, per-message retries, simple scaling.

analogy.title: A recorded broadcast versus a to-do list
analogy.story: The broadcast can be rewatched by anyone; to-do items are ticked off and gone.
analogy.breaks: Broadcasts are watched passively; consumers must track their own checkpoints.

example.title: Two decisions
flow: Clickstream for analytics, ML and alerts → Kinesis

steps.label: Lesson
steps.detail: Events to many readers vs tasks to workers.

check.q: Which service lets a new consumer replay last week's data?
check.a: Kinesis Data Streams (within the retention period).
